input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: Argument.get_help_record returns self.help unchanged, so the second element of the tuple is None for an undocumented argument even though format_arguments now feeds every record straight into formatter.write_dl without a fallback.
- failure path: A command declares two arguments and sets help on only one; running it with --help makes write_dl measure and wrap a None description and the help command crashes with a TypeError instead of printing usage.

Reviewer finding
- description: Argument.get_help_record now always returns a tuple, but when help is None it returns (metavar, None) instead of an empty description string as the docstring and commit title promise. The removed fallback in format_options that substituted "" is gone too.
- rationale: Trigger: a command has one Argument with help set, so the Positional arguments section is rendered, plus another Argument with no help. The second argument yields (metavar, None). HelpFormatter.write_dl then passes None into text wrapping (wrap_text calls expandtabs on the description), which raises AttributeError, or otherwise renders a bogus row. Impact: --help crashes or misprints for any command that mixes documented and undocumented positional arguments, a common pattern.
critique: Both describe the same defect: Argument.get_help_record returns (metavar, None) for an undocumented argument, and the removed fallback lets write_dl wrap None. The result is that --help crashes when a command mixes documented and undocumented arguments. The finding names AttributeError where the label says TypeError, but the operation and the failure path are the same.
